topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class, frames the complexity and importance of complement, and introduces the session.

topics.label: Foundational principles of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the core concepts, structural logic, naming conventions, and central role of C3 in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three pathways that detect targets and trigger complement activation up to the threshold of convertase formation.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the downstream immune outcomes mediated by activated complement products, including opsonization, inflammation, and membrane lysis.

topics.label: Regulation of complement and host protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic focuses on the regulatory mechanisms that prevent complement activation from damaging host tissues.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the diverse clinical presentations and disease susceptibilities resulting from genetic or acquired complement deficiencies.

topics.label: Pathogen strategies for complement evasion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how pathogens evolve specialized mechanisms to circumvent complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Lecture wrap-up and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the discussion on complement and outlines the topic for the subsequent lecture.
